clue.text: These skinny Venuses

parts.note: the lifelike beauties are made from skins, so the people who shape them out of hides are the ones meant

explanation.surface: A remark about some very thin goddesses of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like 'thin' but means 'made of skin': these craftsmen remove and mount skins to make lifelike figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who stuff and mount animal skins create lifelike figures, the 'Venuses' made of skin.

clue.text: Marigold, get into the back seat

indicators.note: the word get is put inside the turned word
back tells us the word for seat runs backwards

explanation.surface: Advice to a gardener with marigolds to climb into the rear of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the seat word round to TAES, and 'into' places the verb inside it; 'Marigold' leads, so the definition is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagetes is the botanical genus of African and French marigolds.

clue.text: Cross east with the French beak by boat

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
bec is French for beak

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses eastward by ship with a French magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate, but here it is a bird's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A xebec is a small three-masted Mediterranean sailing vessel.

clue.text: Sold by Gilpin

parts.note: John Gilpin in Cowper's comic ballad was a linen-draper

explanation.surface: A note on what a particular shopkeeper sold.
explanation.walkthrough: In William Cowper's ballad, John Gilpin is a London linen-draper, so his wares are cloth hangings.
explanation.definitionFit: A draper sells cloth, and hanging fabrics are the goods of that trade.

clue.text: Long depressions — these longings for roe

definitions.meaning: furrows worn into a road or track
the mating urges of deer such as the roe

explanation.definitionFit: Grooves worn by wheels; also the seasonal mating heat of stags seeking roe deer.

clue.text: The King and I put up and turned down by the Gallery -does that annoy !

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up reverses the letters

parts.note: R for rex, king, plus I
the same R and I again, this time read straight down
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Seeing a musical rejected by an art gallery is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' is used twice: 'put up' (in a down clue, read upward) and then 'turned down', set downward as written; the musical's title is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to vex or bother someone.

clue.text: Nothing in the cart perhaps but "a wicked pack of cards"

indicators.note: the round letter for nothing goes inside the reworked word
perhaps says cart may be shuffled into another order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty cart, but a deck of cards described as wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes TARC from CART; 'in' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Taroc is the old tarot pack, whose cards are linked with fortune-telling and so called wicked.

clue.text: Eccentrics all on one side of the street?

definitions.text: Eccentrics all on one side of the street?

parts.words: Eccentrics all on one side of the street?
parts.note: houses numbered 1, 3, 5 and so on line one side of a street

explanation.surface: All the strange people live on one side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd numbers are on one side of a street, so the odd ones are the eccentrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or peculiar people are odd characters, curiosities.

clue.text: But it's not mounted on a fighter plane

definitions.text: But it's not mounted on a fighter plane

parts.words: But it's not mounted on a fighter plane
parts.note: a weapon whose name suggests aircraft but which fires by compressed gas

explanation.surface: A remark that some weapon isn't fitted to a warplane.
explanation.walkthrough: The name suggests an aircraft's weapon, but it is a pellet gun powered by compressed air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet rifle powered by compressed gas, not by explosive, nothing to do with aircraft.

clue.text: Red, white and blue geological specimen

definitions.text: Red, white and blue geological specimen

parts.words: Red, white and blue geological specimen
parts.note: a patriotic British piece of rock, coloured like the Union flag

explanation.surface: A stone sample coloured like a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rock is the nickname of this British territory at the tip of Spain; red, white and blue are the colours of the Union flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The British overseas territory is famous as 'the Rock', so it is a British-flagged rock.

clue.text: More than one spoke out from the heart

definitions.text: More than one spoke out from the heart

parts.words: More than one spoke out from the heart
parts.note: lines running from the centre of a circle like wheel spokes, plural

explanation.surface: Several people talked sincerely, from the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past tense of speak and 'heart' like feelings; really they are wheel spokes and the centre of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines drawn from a circle's centre to its rim are plural of the geometric radius, like spokes.

clue.text: One could get punched during training

definitions.text: One could get punched during training

parts.words: One could get punched during training
parts.note: read 'training' as 'travelling by train', where an inspector clips a pass

explanation.surface: A boxer in training risks being hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' suggests boxing practice, but split it as 'train-ing': on a train a guard punches a hole in your pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail pass was traditionally clipped with a hole by the guard on the journey.

clue.text: Keeping somewhat to the leg

definitions.meaning: holding goods in store, as a shop does
a garment fitted to the leg, a hose

explanation.definitionFit: A shop holds goods in supply; the noun is also hosiery covering the leg.

clue.text: Is baby-minder or registers student's protest

definitions.meaning: minds children while parents are out, babysits
occupies a building in protest, the classic student demonstration

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to babysit and to stage an occupation protest.

clue.text: Lucky. Waverley

explanation.definitionFit: An amulet thought to bring good fortune; also Walter Scott's crusader novel in the Waverley series.

clue.text: The horse stands high in a Swiss city

indicators.note: the word for high is placed inside the Swiss city's name

parts.note: Sion is a city in the Swiss Valais
high means tall

explanation.surface: A horse rears up tall in a city in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands' is a link word, though it tempts as STALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding is a kind of horse.

clue.text: Soldier-statesman there in France yet beset by fate

parts.note: la is French for there

indicators.note: the word yet is surrounded by the word fate

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier and politician in France, still dogged by destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Lafayette was a French general in the American Revolution and later a politician.

clue.text: He was shuttled ? Fought

definitions.meaning: a cock used in a game, the shuttlecock, batted back and forth
a fighting bird bred for cockfights

explanation.definitionFit: A bird bred for cockfighting; also, read in two parts, a feathered cock used in a racket game.

clue.text: Pat or Thales going far to meet a Scot

parts.note: going a long way, many miles
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: An Irishman or a Greek philosopher travels a long way to meet a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both Irish (from the legendary Milesius, so 'Pat') and a native of Miletus, home of the philosopher Thales.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irishman, descended from the legendary King Milesius, or a citizen of Miletus such as Thales.

clue.text: Pre-talkies actor

parts.note: a player in a silent show, before sound films; mum means silent

explanation.surface: A star of the silent cinema era.
explanation.walkthrough: Talkies suggest films, but this is a traditional masked player in a silent folk play; 'mum' means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in traditional mime plays acts without words, as silent-film stars did.

clue.text: Compensation for out-of-form tennis

parts.note: playing badly means being off
a set is a unit of play in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player seeks consolation after a poor display.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterbalancing amount that cancels a loss is a form of compensation.

clue.text: VAT employee ?

parts.note: a worker who crushes grapes underfoot in a tub

explanation.surface: Someone who works on Value Added Tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like the British sales tax, so a tax inspector or trader; but it is a tub where grapes are crushed by foot.
explanation.definitionFit: One who crushes grapes underfoot in a wine tub, stepping on them.

clue.text: Assent to me being involved in music-making

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Agreeing to take part in a musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved' turns ASSENT and ME into the name; the definition loosely points to a composer, Jules Massenet, as a maker of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was a French opera composer, a man whose work was creating music.

clue.text: Quarter-mile perhaps from the tree it comes

parts.note: E, east, is a quarter of the compass

indicators.note: perhaps tells us these letters may be put in another order

explanation.surface: Something that comes from a tree about a quarter-mile away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles E and MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin obtained from tropical trees.

clue.text: B of PBS

parts.note: the middle initial of the poet Percy B. Shelley

explanation.surface: A question about the letters of a broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: PBS looks like the American broadcaster, but it is the poet Percy Bysshe Shelley's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Shelley's middle name, standing behind the B of his initials.

clue.text: Horsy Rupert's sweetheart

indicators.note: the possessive reads as 'has', the phrase holding the letters

explanation.surface: A horse-loving man named Rupert has a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit at the very heart of 'Horsy Rupert'; the clue's last word is read as 'sweet heart', a sweet thing found in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick sugary liquid is a sweet thing, read from the word 'sweetheart'.

clue.text: Uncorrect Latin

parts.note: the Latin word a proof-reader writes to cancel a correction, meaning let it stand

explanation.surface: A complaint about bad Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncorrect' looks like 'incorrect', but it means 'undo a correction': proof-readers write this Latin word to restore the original.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin proof mark meaning 'let it stand' undoes an editor's change.

clue.text: Cancel ? Right, no difficulty about 'that

indicators.note: the phrase for no difficulty goes around the letter for right

parts.note: ease is freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: Calling something off with no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out or delete something is to cancel it.

clue.text: Wasn't glaringly introverted; caused eyes to turn

definitions.meaning: glared outward rather than inward, read as out + glared
won a staring match, making the rival look away

explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone in a staring contest makes them look away; read in parts, it is gazing outward.

clue.text: He could let the side down, by the bye

definitions.text: He could let the side down, by the bye

parts.words: He could let the side down, by the bye
parts.note: byes in cricket are runs conceded when the ball passes the stumps unstopped

explanation.surface: A passing remark that someone might disappoint the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the bye' looks like 'incidentally', but in cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball beats the player behind the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketer behind the stumps is blamed when byes are conceded, letting the team down.
